A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching core methods, theorem numbering and proofs. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, including v2’s added Appendices B and C.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical guarantees, counterexamples and proofs. Neither its main text nor Appendix A reports original empirical or simulation outcomes.

after.justification: V2 Appendix C and Table 1 report original synthetic contextual-bandit experiments comparing truthful and strategic labeling across four sample sizes.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the MLE, confidence-set, median and pessimistic policy-optimization pipeline. Appendix B adds a penalty-based approximate inner optimization in Equations (7)–(8), projected-gradient procedures and parameterized-policy adaptations, constituting a limited computational extension.

E1.justification: V1 has no empirical dataset or task coverage. V2 adds synthetic contextual-bandit evaluation with heterogeneous Gaussian-drawn reward parameters under truthful and strategically optimized feedback. The theoretical MDP coverage does not become an empirical MDP evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 1 introduces empirical comparisons against Naive MLEs, Pessimistic Social Welfare and Median of MLEs. V1’s analytical treatment of Pessimistic Social Welfare and MaxMin-RLHF remains; MaxMin-RLHF is not included in the new experiment.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces a complete new evaluation protocol: d = 16, k = 5, n = 20, 50, 100 and 200, and 200 steps of simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation for strategic reporting. It evaluates the existing suboptimality measure under truthful and strategic labeling; no earlier experimental protocol is replaced.

E4.justification: V2 adds empirical manipulation-robustness tests and sample-size sensitivity analysis. Comparing mean versus median aggregation with and without pessimism also supplies component comparisons absent from v1’s theoretical analysis.

E5.justification: V2 introduces averaging over five random seeds and standard errors throughout Table 1. V1 contains no empirical repeated-run or uncertainty reporting. This is a new statistical reporting practice, not evidence of increased runs for an existing experiment.

E6.justification: All Table 1 results are new. At n = 50, proposed-method suboptimality changes from 0.508 under truthful labeling to 0.532 under strategic labeling, versus 0.403 to 0.652 for Pessimistic Social Welfare. The proposed method is not uniformly best under strategic labeling. At n = 100, Naive MLEs’ reported difference, 0.316, contradicts its displayed means: 0.516 − 0.230 = 0.286.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds concavity derivations, optimization reformulations, Lemma B.1 and its approximation proof, and an MDP occupancy-measure formulation. V2 also explicitly bounds feature norms in Assumption 1 and removes label-sampling expectations from the high-probability inequalities in Theorems 4.1 and 5.1. Most existing Appendix A proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain strategic offline RLHF, manipulability and impossibility results, and approximately strategyproof Pessimistic Median of MLEs with welfare guarantees for contextual bandits and MDPs. The revised abstract restates claims already present in v1; the new appendices do not replace the headline contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of the empirical robustness and sample-size plateau, states applicability to arbitrary misreporting distributions, and discusses computational limitations. Appendix B leaves convergence for parameterized policies unresolved, while Section 6 notes that scaling to LLM fine-tuning may sacrifice theoretical guarantees. These qualify the retained incentive–welfare tradeoff.

D1.justification: V2 adds optimization formulations, penalty-selection guidance, projected-gradient procedures and a specified ridge-regularization order. Appendix C documents Gaussian reward initialization, strategic-update method and budget, dimensions and sample counts. These substantially expand implementation information, although code access and a complete simulation-generation recipe remain absent.

R1.justification: Seven references are added, including PAL, strategic linear contextual bandits, softmax policy-gradient convergence and offline-RL coverage work. They support the expanded discussion, computation and simulation methodology. The positioning against truthful-feedback, adversarial-corruption and payment-based approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract and explanatory paragraphs, expands the motivation for distribution-level strategies, changes Bradley–Terry–Luce terminology to Bradley–Terry, and repairs the unresolved Appendix reference. The main section sequence and Appendix A proof organization remain, with computational and experimental appendices added.

P2.justification: The entire document adopts NeurIPS typography and formatting, with a redesigned title and affiliation block, changed spacing and reflowed equations and proofs. Algorithm 1 is restyled, and a new Table 1 presents four sample-size blocks with means, standard errors and differences. No figures are added.

improvement.justification: V2 improves assessability through computational formulations and an initial empirical robustness check with standard errors, both absent from v1. The gain is limited by the small, incompletely specified simulation and unresolved convergence for parameterized policies. Table 1 also introduces an arithmetic inconsistency: its n = 100 Naive MLEs difference is 0.316 although the displayed means imply 0.286. These limitations temper the useful additions.
